title: Hanno's Carthaginian voyage down the west African coast
summary: A Carthaginian expedition under Hanno, with sixty fifty-oared ships and about thirty thousand men and women according to the Greek text, sailed out past the Pillars of Heracles and south along the west African coast, founding cities on the way. Its date is uncertain, and scholars disagree whether it reached only Sierra Leone or as far as Cameroon or Gabon.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia: the voyage was probably between the late 6th century BCE and c. 425 BCE, and the Punic original was carved on a stele c. 400 BCE. Years are my conversion of "late 6th century" (taken as about 550 BCE) and c. 425 BCE (-424). The Szeged text gives no date.

as_recorded.value: between the late 6th century BCE and c. 425 BCE

reviewer_note: Least sure: how far south the voyage went and every stop beyond Thymiaterion (debated: Sierra Leone vs Cameroon/Gabon). Lixos, Cerne and the Chretes were left out because World History Encyclopedia leaves Cerne unidentified and I found no clean Wikidata point for the river mouths. The date is a range stated by the source; pin is at Carthage, the departure port. Mount Cameroon is a "possibly" identification.
